reference: S. Majumder and S. K. Das, 'Domain coarsening in two dimensions: Conserved dynamics and finite-size scaling', Physical Review E 81, 050102(R) (2010), DOI:10.1103/PhysRevE.81.050102; preprint https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.3985
purpose: Compare two pre-specified operational domain lengths on the same completed 40-run L=128 symmetric Kawasaki trajectories: the archived connected-correlation half-height and a paper-inspired, majority-filtered mean chord length. The aim is to quantify finite-window measurement dependence, not to select the result closest to one third.
dynamics_match: Both studies use a periodic 2D square lattice, symmetric 50:50 composition, conserved nearest-neighbour Kawasaki exchanges, isotropic coupling and T=0.6Tc. This campaign uses Metropolis acceptance, its own random proposal stream, exactly fixed composition, 40 independent random starts, L=128 and 4.5 million attempted-exchange sweeps. The source paper does not specify enough implementation detail to claim identical dynamics. With equilibration=0, this campaign starts from random fixed-composition lattices, not equilibrated 3Tc states.
postprocessing_match: The paper describes replacing each spin by the majority among itself and its four nearest neighbours before measurement. This implementation applies one simultaneous periodic five-site majority pass to each saved snapshot only. The paper does not unambiguously specify pass count or simultaneous versus sequential replacement, so this is a paper-inspired operator rather than a proven exact reconstruction. The filtered image is never fed back into the dynamics and its phase fraction is recorded because the filter need not conserve it.
observable_match: The paper's principal length is the first moment of horizontal and vertical interface-to-interface domain-length distributions. This implementation pools every finite same-spin chord along both periodic axes after one filter pass and reports their arithmetic mean. Uniform scan lines are unresolved and omitted rather than assigned length L. The comparator is the mean of the two archived connected-correlation C(r)=0.5 crossings on the unfiltered snapshot. These are distinct operational lengths; neither is declared the unique physical domain radius.
comparison_scope: Use all 40 completed c=0.5, L=128 trajectories and all saved checkpoints. Report the frozen windows 1000-200000, 1000-4500000 and 200000-4500000 sweeps. Report raw fits and a separately labelled sensitivity that subtracts the measured length at the checkpoint nearest 20 sweeps; do not optimise an offset. Use whole trajectories as bootstrap units, shared resolved-time masks for paired differences, and retain unresolved cases. This single-size comparison cannot reproduce the paper's multi-size collapse or establish finite-size onset.
